objective: Generate, publish, natively compile, run, and package one coherent DomainSpec application with explicitly selected integration realizations while preserving semantic and evidence boundaries.
claim_ceiling: DAG completion may form an exact review candidate. It does not grant admission, publication, release, deployment, production readiness, provider authority, or production runtime guarantees.

execution_policy.failure_mode: Run all checks within the failing node, record causal failures, and mark descendants not_evaluable.
execution_policy.mutation_rule: Write only within the node's declared work package and preserve unrelated dirty bytes.
execution_policy.parallel_rule: Nodes are parallel-ready only when all dependencies pass and their declared write scopes do not overlap.
execution_policy.promotion_rule: A layer is promotable only when its terminal node passes with all required evidence current.
execution_policy.compatibility_rule: Commands without --integration-source retain current behavior and bytes.
execution_policy.cleanup_rule: Disposable outputs, containers, volumes, and per-case dependency caches must be removed before a terminal can pass.

layers.title: TypeScript minimum whole-application proof
layers.decision_question: After this layer, we know whether one TypeScript domain graph and integration graph can form and natively compile as one coherent project.
layers.minimum_working_unit: One joined commerce fixture, exact cross-graph binding, embedded integration contribution, deterministic composition, and tsc --noEmit.
layers.user_outcome: The package API returns one exact TypeScript whole-application plan.

layers.title: Three-language CLI completion
layers.decision_question: After this layer, we know whether whole-application compilation is repeatable through the public CLI for every supported language.
layers.minimum_working_unit: Python and Rust composition, CLI source intake, atomic publication, currentness checks, and clean native verification.
layers.user_outcome: One CLI workflow generates and verifies a complete TypeScript, Python, or Rust project.

layers.title: Explicit reference provider realization
layers.decision_question: After this layer, we know whether explicit provider selections can produce runnable adapter and bootstrap code without redefining domain meaning.
layers.minimum_working_unit: PostgreSQL, NATS JetStream, and HTTP provider packs generated and compiled for all supported languages.
layers.user_outcome: A generated application contains concrete adapters and configuration for one explicitly selected reference stack.

layers.title: Bounded real-runtime proof
layers.decision_question: After this layer, we know whether the generated reference application behaves correctly across real disposable integration boundaries.
layers.minimum_working_unit: Fresh PostgreSQL and NATS services, local HTTP fixtures, one commerce scenario, hostile failures, bounded observations, and cleanup proof.
layers.user_outcome: A locally runnable generated application demonstrates persistence, messaging, and HTTP behavior.

layers.title: Packaging and exact candidate
layers.decision_question: After this layer, we know whether whole-application compilation survives package installation and can be presented as an exact review candidate.
layers.minimum_working_unit: Complete package assets, installed commerce example, three-language consumer verification, documentation, and a frozen candidate.
layers.user_outcome: A consumer can install the candidate and reproduce the documented whole-application flows.

nodes.title: Freeze the application and integration predecessor surfaces
outputs: Predecessor inventory with source, schema, layout, public API, toolchain, and exact integration-candidate digests
nodes.done_when: One current inventory uniquely identifies every predecessor consumed by L0.
stop_conditions: Overlapping active writer on required bytes

nodes.title: Define the closed application-to-integration binding contract
checks: Entity, value object, enum, sum, interface, operation, event, mapping, and failure references have declared expected kinds
Provider identifiers cannot satisfy domain references
nodes.done_when: Every cross-graph reference family has one explicit target kind and failure code.
stop_conditions: A required join has no canonical DomainSpec representation
Contract would introduce a new domain meta-type

nodes.title: Create one joined commerce source fixture
outputs: Commerce integration source whose domain references resolve against the installed reconciled-commerce graph
checks: No suffix or unqualified lookup is required
nodes.done_when: The fixture is exact, self-contained, and covers persistence, messaging, APIs, mappings, failures, and observation.
stop_conditions: Current commerce source lacks an essential declared boundary

nodes.title: Implement exact typed cross-graph resolution
checks: Domain source and integration digests are bound
No source re-read after checked snapshot
nodes.done_when: A valid pair yields one immutable binding receipt and every invalid join fails before generation.

nodes.title: Extract embedded TypeScript integration contributions
checks: No standalone tsconfig is emitted in embedded mode
Child plan is frozen and deterministic
nodes.done_when: The existing integration source produces a responsibility-owned TypeScript contribution without publication or root ownership.
stop_conditions: Embedded mode requires changing standalone output

nodes.title: Implement TypeScript artifact and manifest composition
checks: No artifact content is silently overwritten
nodes.done_when: Application and embedded integration artifacts compose into one closed TypeScript artifact inventory.
stop_conditions: Merge requires in-place file mutation without structural ownership

nodes.title: Form the public whole-application plan
checks: Only registered current child plans accepted
Binding and both plan digests are retained
nodes.done_when: The joined commerce inputs form one exact public TypeScript application plan.
stop_conditions: Plan identity can omit a child or binding digest

nodes.title: Prove semantic and structural non-collapse
outputs: Hostile binding, ownership, collision, and claim-boundary test report
checks: Missing, extra, wrong-kind, case-drifted, and ambiguous references reject
Queue, topic, stream, and dead-letter remain distinct
nodes.done_when: Every enumerated hostile mutation produces the expected causal failure before output effects.
stop_conditions: Failure is non-causal or occurs after publication

nodes.title: Prove deterministic TypeScript native compilation
checks: Repeated and multiprocess plans are byte-identical
Temporary roots and per-case caches are absent after the run
nodes.done_when: The same inputs repeatedly produce one natively compilable TypeScript project and leave no residue.

nodes.title: Join L0 evidence and decide L1 eligibility
outputs: L0 completion receipt with exact source, test, compiler, artifact, and claim-ceiling bindings
checks: No L1 or runtime claim is present
nodes.done_when: L0 is complete and the TypeScript composition contract is frozen for L1.
stop_conditions: Any L0 node failed or is not_evaluable

nodes.title: Freeze the passed L0 composition contract
outputs: L1 predecessor manifest binding the L0 receipt and public composer surface
checks: L0 source and artifacts are current
Python and Rust toolchains are pinned
nodes.done_when: L1 has one immutable predecessor and language denominator.

nodes.title: Implement embedded Python composition
checks: Standalone Python integration output remains unchanged
nodes.done_when: The joined commerce source forms one import-closed Python project plan.

nodes.title: Implement embedded Rust composition
checks: All files are reachable from lib.rs
Standalone Rust integration output remains unchanged
nodes.done_when: The joined commerce source forms one module-closed Rust crate plan.

nodes.title: Join cross-language semantic equivalence
checks: Language-specific paths do not change meaning
All three artifact inventories are deterministic
nodes.done_when: TypeScript, Python, and Rust represent the same joined application and integration graph.

nodes.title: Add fail-closed CLI integration-source intake
checks: Duplicate, partial, unknown, and conflicting options reject before source reads
Calls without the option follow the existing path
nodes.done_when: The CLI selects integration-aware planning only from one explicit valid option set.
stop_conditions: Invalid input can reach target writes

nodes.title: Publish one exact whole-application target
checks: Target is normalized, absolute, and new
All bytes match the registered plan
Race and collision failures are causal
nodes.done_when: instantiate-project and build publish one exact target and combined receipt for each language.
stop_conditions: Partial public target can be mistaken for complete
Publication accepts a serialized unregistered plan

nodes.title: Implement exact source and artifact currentness
checks: Domain, selection, integration, layout, receipt, and artifact drift are independent checks
nodes.done_when: verify detects every selected stale-input and output mutation without rewriting the target.

nodes.title: Run stronger native verification for all languages
outputs: TypeScript, Python, and Rust native compile reports with pinned tool identities
checks: Cargo check passes offline with locked inputs
nodes.done_when: Every published language target passes its native compiler from exact original bytes.

nodes.title: Prove CLI compatibility and clean-consumer operation
checks: Invalid and incomplete results are nonzero
nodes.done_when: The additive CLI surface works for all three languages without changing existing behavior.

nodes.title: Join L1 evidence and decide provider-realization eligibility
outputs: L1 completion receipt binding three languages, CLI, publication, currentness, native tools, and compatibility
nodes.done_when: Whole-application native compilation is complete for TypeScript, Python, and Rust.

nodes.title: Freeze the passed three-language whole-application surface
outputs: L2 predecessor manifest and explicit reference-stack denominator
checks: No provider is selected by default
nodes.done_when: L2 starts from one current compiler surface and one non-default reference stack.

nodes.title: Define the provider-pack selection contract
checks: Provider data cannot add domain semantics
nodes.done_when: Each provider selection resolves one compatible language realization or one causal failure.
stop_conditions: Provider contract needs authority over workflows or rules

nodes.title: Compose provider dependencies and root manifests
checks: Root manifest ownership remains with the composer
nodes.done_when: Provider packs can declare deterministic dependencies and module contributions without editing child artifacts.

nodes.title: Generate the TypeScript reference provider pack
checks: Failures map only to declared outcomes
No business rule appears in provider code
nodes.done_when: The explicit TypeScript reference selection emits a complete compilable adapter set.

nodes.title: Generate the Python reference provider pack
checks: Failures map only to declared outcomes
No business rule appears in provider code
nodes.done_when: The explicit Python reference selection emits a complete compilable adapter set.

nodes.title: Generate the Rust reference provider pack
checks: Failures map only to declared outcomes
No business rule appears in provider code
nodes.done_when: The explicit Rust reference selection emits a complete compilable adapter set.

nodes.title: Compose bootstrap, migration, and configuration entry points
checks: Missing configuration fails without secret disclosure
No external call occurs during planning
nodes.done_when: Each language project has one compilable entry point that wires the selected providers without executing them at generation time.

nodes.title: Prove provider selection and secret boundaries
outputs: Dependency absence report for unselected packs
checks: Unselected code and dependencies are absent
Credential values never enter plans, artifacts, diagnostics, or receipts
nodes.done_when: All provider and credential boundary mutations fail causally before publication or startup.

nodes.title: Compile the complete reference provider matrix
outputs: Locked TypeScript, Python, and Rust provider compilation reports
checks: All imports resolve from declared dependencies
No runtime service is required for compilation
nodes.done_when: All three complete applications compile with the explicitly selected reference providers.

nodes.title: Join L2 evidence and decide runtime-proof eligibility
outputs: L2 completion receipt binding provider selections, generated adapters, dependency locks, and native compile evidence
nodes.done_when: Concrete provider code is generated and compiled without a runtime-behavior claim.
stop_conditions: Compile evidence is reported as runtime evidence

nodes.title: Freeze the compiled reference application and runtime denominator
outputs: Pinned PostgreSQL, NATS, HTTP fixture, and application tool identities
checks: Container and tool images are exact
nodes.done_when: One disposable runtime environment can be created without host-global state.
stop_conditions: Broad or shared destructive cleanup target

nodes.title: Implement the disposable runtime harness
outputs: Unique network, container, volume, process, and temporary-root lifecycle
checks: All resources carry a run identifier
nodes.done_when: The harness can create and completely remove an isolated empty environment.
stop_conditions: Cleanup requires a broad wildcard or shared volume deletion

nodes.title: Define the runtime scenario and evidence contract
checks: Provider acceptance, delivery, commit, and business completion are separate
Every assertion names its evidence source
nodes.done_when: Success and failure scenarios have bounded expected observations before services run.
stop_conditions: Expected behavior is absent from declared domain or integration sources

nodes.title: Bring up and qualify fresh PostgreSQL
nodes.done_when: The generated migration launcher creates the expected schema in a fresh database.

nodes.title: Bring up and qualify fresh NATS JetStream
outputs: Declared stream, topic, queue consumer, and dead-letter resources
checks: Ordering, acknowledgement, and deduplication settings remain distinct
nodes.done_when: The generated messaging bootstrap creates exactly the declared broker resources.
stop_conditions: Channel kind is emulated by relabeling another kind
Shared pre-existing broker state is required

nodes.title: Bring up and qualify local HTTP boundaries
nodes.done_when: Both HTTP directions are reachable only inside the disposable harness.

nodes.title: Start the generated application against qualified services
checks: Health does not imply business completion
nodes.done_when: The application reaches its declared ready state from generated bytes and explicit configuration.

nodes.title: Execute the successful commerce scenario
checks: OrderSubmitted maps to a distinct Message
Outbound HTTP result maps into the application boundary
Each receipt stops at its observed stage
nodes.done_when: One operation completes with mutually consistent domain, database, broker, HTTP, and receipt evidence.
stop_conditions: Evidence is inferred rather than observed

nodes.title: Execute bounded provider and application failures
outputs: Rollback, provider rejection, retry classification, dead-letter, and invalid-webhook evidence
checks: Provider failure maps to a declared outcome
Invalid signature reaches no application operation
nodes.done_when: Every selected failure produces its declared bounded outcome and no extra effect.
stop_conditions: Automatic continuation is selected by D48
Failure leaks secret or inflates evidence

nodes.title: Project disclosure-bounded observations to ORODI
checks: No retry, provider write, API call, deployment, or business effect capability exists
nodes.done_when: ORODI receives complete bounded observation inputs and cannot influence runtime behavior.
stop_conditions: Any control or return edge exists

nodes.title: Dispose and audit all runtime resources
outputs: Post-run filesystem, process, container, volume, and port audit
checks: Owned containers, network, and volumes removed
nodes.done_when: The host returns to its pre-run owned-resource state with evidence.
stop_conditions: Cleanup target cannot be proven owned

nodes.title: Join L3 runtime evidence and decide packaging eligibility
outputs: L3 completion receipt binding exact generated bytes, runtime environment, success/failure observations, and cleanup
checks: Claims do not exceed observed stages
nodes.done_when: The reference application has bounded real-runtime evidence and no remaining owned runtime resources.

nodes.title: Freeze the passed runtime candidate inputs
outputs: L4 predecessor manifest and exact package-input allowlist
nodes.done_when: Packaging starts from one exact source and evidence frontier.

nodes.title: Define the installed whole-application package surface
checks: No evidence or secret fixture is accidentally packed
nodes.done_when: The intended installed surface is exact and machine-checkable.
stop_conditions: Consumer flow depends on an unpacked or checkout-only file

nodes.title: Package schemas, compiler surfaces, and provider packs
checks: Provider resources match their source hashes
nodes.done_when: All non-example runtime and compiler assets are present under installed-package paths.

nodes.title: Package the joined commerce example and user documentation
checks: Commands are copyable from a clean consumer
Compile and runtime claims are distinguished
No open product questions or internal-only instructions
nodes.done_when: A user can follow one coherent path from authored sources through generation, compile, startup, runtime observation, and verification.

nodes.title: Build and audit the package tarball
checks: No temporary, cache, development, credential, or untracked evidence residue
Package metadata and bin targets resolve
nodes.done_when: One exact package tarball passes the clean-package contract.

nodes.title: Run the installed TypeScript consumer flow
outputs: Fresh-install TypeScript generation, native compile, startup, scenario, and verification report
nodes.done_when: A fresh consumer reproduces the complete documented TypeScript flow.

nodes.title: Run the installed Python consumer flow
outputs: Fresh-install Python generation, native compile, startup, scenario, and verification report
nodes.done_when: A fresh consumer reproduces the complete documented Python flow.

nodes.title: Run the installed Rust consumer flow
outputs: Fresh-install Rust generation, native compile, startup, scenario, and verification report
nodes.done_when: A fresh consumer reproduces the complete documented Rust flow.

nodes.title: Freeze the exact whole-application candidate
outputs: Exact candidate manifest binding sources, generated artifacts, package, tests, runtime evidence, environment, and claim ceiling
checks: All bound files exist and hash current
Test denominator has no omitted required property
Compiler and provider identities are pinned
nodes.done_when: One immutable candidate uniquely identifies the reviewed product bytes and evidence.
stop_conditions: Any binding is stale or missing

nodes.title: Independently review candidate completeness and claim boundaries
outputs: Read-only review report with pass, fail, or not_evaluable for every candidate obligation
nodes.done_when: An independent read-only review accounts for every required obligation and discrepancy.
stop_conditions: Evidence is accepted by assertion alone

nodes.title: Join the complete DAG as a review-ready product candidate
outputs: Whole-application completion receipt and product-review handoff
checks: Every DAG node is passed and represented
nodes.done_when: The whole-application capability is a complete exact candidate ready for product review.
stop_conditions: Any node failed or is not_evaluable
Any admission, release, deployment, or production inference
